title: Sikkim — the complete guide
selection: Sikkim had 13 places, one itinerary and one guide. This pack adds Gangtok's sights, the Old Silk Route (Zuluk, Nathang, Aritar), South Sikkim (Namchi, Ravangla, Temi), West Sikkim's old capitals and monasteries (Rabdentse, Yuksom, Dubdi, Tashiding, Goecha La) and North Sikkim (Lachen, Chungthang, Singba), with 4 itineraries and 9 guides — researched from Incredible India (Ministry of Tourism) and Wikipedia.

ST_PERMIT.claim: Many areas of Sikkim are restricted and need permits.

evidence.quote: Many areas are restricted, and permits are needed to visit them.

ST_MONSOON.claim: Sikkim has five seasons; monsoon rains raise the risk of landslides, which can cut off towns.

evidence.quote: The state has five seasons: winter, summer, spring, autumn, and monsoon season.
During the monsoon, heavy rains increase the risk of landslides .
landslides are frequent, often isolating rural towns and villages from the major urban centres

ST_FEST.claim: Festivals include Losar (Tibetan New Year), Saga Dawa, Pang Lhabsol for Sikkim's guardian deities, and the Sakewa festival.

evidence.quote: Losar, the Tibetan New Year, paints the state in vibrant hues.
Pang Lhabsol pays homage to Sikkim's guardian deities.
the Sakewa festival worships Mother Earth

ST_FOOD.claim: Try momos, thukpa and gundruk, bamboo-shoot dishes, millet dishes and yak-butter tea.

evidence.quote: sample traditional delicacies like momos, thukpa, and gundruk
fragrant bamboo shoot delicacies and traditional millet-based dishes
dishes such as momos, thukpa, and yak butter tea

ST_ADV.claim: Rafting on the Teesta, paragliding, hiking and mountain biking are popular.

evidence.quote: The Teesta River provides an exhilarating opportunity for river rafting.
Adventure sports like paragliding , hiking , and mountain biking are also popular in Sikkim.

ST_FLORA.claim: The noble dendrobium orchid is the state flower and the rhododendron the state tree; spring brings rhododendron and primrose blooms.

evidence.quote: The Noble Dendrobium is the official flower of Sikkim, while the rhododendron is the state tree .
If you are here during spring, you will be blessed with a massive stretch of rhododendron blooms and delicate primroses.

MGM1.claim: MG Marg, Gangtok's main promenade, is lined with shops selling handicrafts and fashion, and cafés.

evidence.quote: Take a stroll through MG Marg, the city's main promenade, and lose yourself in a sea of shops selling everything from traditional handicrafts to contemporary fashion

ENC1.claim: Enchey, 'the Solitary Monastery', sits on a ridge above Gangtok with views of the Kanchenjunga range.

evidence.quote: The literal meaning of Enchey Monastery is the "Solitary Monastery".
The monastery is built on a stunning ridge of a hill above the Gangtok city to its northeast from where the Kanchendzonga range is visible.

HAN1.claim: Hanuman Tok above Gangtok is a Hanuman temple maintained by the Indian Army.

evidence.quote: The temple is dedicated to lord Hanuman , and maintained by the Indian army .

DOD1.claim: The Do-drul Chorten stupa in Gangtok was built in 1945–46; its gilded top crowns a white base ringed by prayer wheels.

evidence.quote: Construction began in 1945 and was completed the following year.
the exterior is topped by a gilded metal cap, while the base is painted white, symbolizing purity
Devotees spin these wheels in a clockwise direction while circumambulating

RAF1.claim: Teesta rafting suits beginners and experienced rafters, through forests, villages and gorges.

evidence.quote: The turbulent waters of the Teesta offer various levels of difficulty, making it suitable for both beginners and seasoned rafters.
The Teesta River Rafting experience takes you through dense forests, quaint villages, and awe-inspiring gorges

FAM1.claim: Fambong Lho Wildlife Sanctuary, about 20 km from Gangtok, is good for hiking.

evidence.quote: consider hiking in the Fambong Lho Wildlife Sanctuary, about 20km away from Gangtok

BAB1.claim: Baba Mandir near Nathu La honours Harbhajan Singh, a soldier who died near the pass in 1968; soldiers believe he still guards it.

evidence.quote: Singh died in 1968 near the Nathu La (pass) in eastern Sikkim
There is a temple dedicated to him in East Sikkim.
He is said to serve the Indian Army even after his death by coming in dreams of soldiers and telling them the plans of their enemies.

ZUL1.claim: Zuluk, at about 9,400 ft, was a stop on the old trade route between Kalimpong and Tibet and now draws visitors for its Himalayan views.

evidence.quote: Dzuluk is at an altitude of about 9,400 feet.
Dzuluk was once a transit point to the trade route between Kalimpong and Tibet.
Today it is a tourist destination for the view of the eastern Himalayan mountain range including the Kanchenjunga .

ZUL2.claim: Zuluk is on NH-717B via Rongli, about 7 hours from Siliguri; winter brings 3–5 ft of snow.

evidence.quote: Dzuluk lies on the National Highway-717B connecting Rhenock and Menla, via Rongli .
Dzuluk can be reached from Siliguri by various hired vehicle in roughly 7 hours.
The winter may see snowfall in the area of about 3–5 feet

NAT1.claim: Tibetan and British forces clashed at Gnathang (Nathang) on 22 May 1888.

evidence.quote: On 22 May 1888 Tibetan and British forces clashed at Gnathong

ARI1.claim: Aritar has Lampokhari, one of Sikkim's oldest natural lakes and its only boating lake (4,600 ft), and an 1895 British dak bungalow.

evidence.quote: Lampokhari is one of the oldest natural lakes in Sikkim
At an altitude of 4600 ft (1,400 m) it is the only boat-ready lake in Sikkim.
an old British-built dak bungalow built by Sir James Claude White

NAM1.claim: Namchi has a 135 ft statue of Guru Padmasambhava; Siddhesvara Dham is about 5 km away on Solophok hill.

evidence.quote: standing at 135 ft (41 m) tall
Siddhesvara Dham is located atop Solophok hilltop, about 5 km (3.1 mi) from Namchi.

NAM2.claim: New Jalpaiguri railway station is about 96 km from Namchi; Bagdogra airport about 102 km.

evidence.quote: The nearest major railhead is located at New Jalpaiguri , about 96 km (60 mi) from the town.
The nearest airport is the Bagdogra airport in West Bengal, located about 102 km

RAV1.claim: Ravangla is about 61 km from Gangtok and 120 km from Siliguri.

evidence.quote: It is approximately 61 km from the state capital, Gangtok , and 120 km from Siliguri , West Bengal .

BUD1.claim: Buddha Park (Tathagata Tsal) near Ravangla has a 130 ft copper statue of the Buddha, consecrated by the Dalai Lama in 2013.

evidence.quote: The Buddha Park of Ravangla , also known as Tathagata Tsal
features a 130-foot-high (40 m) statue of the Buddha
The statue, built of 60 tonnes of copper
the statue was consecrated on 25 March 2013 by the 14th Dalai Lama

TEM1.claim: Temi Tea Garden, set up in 1969 on 177 hectares, grows organic tea sold as 'Temi Tea'.

evidence.quote: The Temi Tea estate was established in 1969 covering an area of 177 hectares
The tea produced in this garden is also partly marketed under the trade name "Temi Tea".

RAB1.claim: Rabdentse, near Pelling, was Sikkim's second royal capital after Yuksom; Gurkha invaders destroyed it, leaving palace ruins and chortens with Kanchenjunga views.

evidence.quote: The reign of the Chogyal was peaceful and saw the capital shifted from Yuksom to Rabdentse.
The capital city was destroyed by the invading Gurkha army and only the ruins of the palace and the chortens are seen here now.
From the vantage point of this former capital, superb views of the Khanchendzonga ranges can be witnessed.

YUK1.claim: Yuksom was Sikkim's first capital, founded in 1642; the first Chogyal was crowned at Norbugang Chorten. It is the base for Kanchenjunga treks.

evidence.quote: It was the first capital of the Kingdom of Sikkim , established in 1642 by Phuntsog Namgyal , the first Chogyal of Sikkim.
Yuksom is home to the Norbugang Chorten , the stupa where Namgyal was crowned.
it attracts mountaineers and trekkers from around the world

DUB1.claim: Dubdi, 'the retreat', near Yuksom, was Sikkim's first monastery (1701), at 2,100 m; tell the resident monk before you visit.

evidence.quote: The Chogyal established Sikkim's first monastery at Yuksom, known as the Dubdi Monastery , in 1701.
Dubdi stands at an altitude of 2,100 metres
the only monk who stays in the monastery has to be informed in advance

GOE1.claim: Goecha La pass faces Kanchenjunga's south-east face; the trek is demanding and acclimatisation matters.

evidence.quote: The southeast face of Kanchenjunga , the world's third highest mountain, can be viewed from the pass
The trek itself can be challenging in terms of distances to be covered in a day.
Acclimatization is important due to the huge changes in altitude over a small time during this trek.

TAS1.claim: Tashiding Monastery, founded in 1641, sits on a hill 19 km south-east of Yuksom; its Bumchu holy-water festival falls around February–March.

evidence.quote: the monastery by this name was founded in 1641
19 kilometres (12 mi) to the south east of Yuksam
The annual festival of Bumchu, meaning ~Holy water~ takes place on the 14th and 15th of the 1st month of Tibetan lunar calendar, often around the months of February and March.

LCH1.claim: Lachen, at about 9,600 ft and 129 km from Gangtok, is the base for Gurudongmar Lake; the village is run by its traditional Dzumsa council.

evidence.quote: 129 km from Gangtok , Lachen sits at an elevation of about 9,600 feet
Lachen is notable for its traditional self-governing system known as Dzumsa
Lachen is the base for visits to: Gurudongmar Lake

LCH2.claim: Thangu valley, 30 km north of Lachen, has summer wildflowers; Chopta suits trekking and birdwatching.

evidence.quote: Thangu Valley– Located 30 km north, it offers accommodation options and is adorned with wildflowers during the summer and monsoon.
Chopta is ideal for trekking, birdwatching, and wildlife spotting.

CHU1.claim: Chungthang, 95 km from Gangtok, is where the Lachen and Lachung rivers meet to form the Teesta.

evidence.quote: It is situated at the confluence of the Lachen and Lachung rivers, which combine to form the Teesta River .
Located at a distance of 95 kilometres

SIN1.claim: The Singba sanctuary has over 40 rhododendron species that bloom each spring, with red pandas and Himalayan black bears.

evidence.quote: The Singba Rhododendron Sanctuary is a living canvas adorned with over 40 species of rhododendron flowers
transforms the forest into a riot of colours each spring
such as the adorable Red Panda, the elusive Himalayan Black Bear

RLL1.claim: Rong Lungten Lee is a museum built as a traditional Lepcha house where the Teesta and Kanaka rivers meet.

evidence.quote: this museum is modelled after a traditional Lepcha house and is situated at the confluence of the Teesta and Kanaka rivers

N_SK1.claim: Sikkim is home to Kanchenjunga, the world's third-highest mountain and India's highest, and to the UNESCO-listed Khangchendzonga National Park.

evidence.quote: It is home to the Kanchenjunga National Park , a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and boasts the Kanchenjunga Peak, India's loftiest summit.
offers stunning views of the Kanchenjunga range, the world’s third-highest mountain.

N_SK2.claim: Sikkim has banned plastic water bottles, one of India's most environmentally conscious states.

evidence.quote: Sikkim has demonstrated its commitment to environmental conservation by prohibiting the use of plastic water bottles

N_SK3.claim: Sikkimese food blends Tibetan, Nepali and Lepcha cooking; it is also home to the fiery Dalle Khorsani chilli.

evidence.quote: Sikkimese food is a harmonious fusion of Tibetan, Nepali, and Lepcha influences
The state is renowned for producing the scorching hot Dalle Khorsani chili

N_SK4.claim: The Indian Army controls large border areas of Sikkim; many are restricted and need permits.

evidence.quote: The Indian Army has control of a large territory, as the state is a sensitive border area. Many areas are restricted, and permits are needed to visit them.

N_SK5.claim: Bagdogra airport near Siliguri is the gateway to Gangtok; Sikkim's Pakyong airport has no operating flights at present.

evidence.quote: It is the gateway to the hill stations of Darjeeling , Gangtok , Kurseong , Kalimpong , Mirik
However, the resumption proved short lived and at present there are no operational flights from Pakyong.

N_GT1.claim: Gangtok, Sikkim's capital, sits at 1,650 m with a mild climate — about 22°C at most in summer and 5°C at night in winter.

evidence.quote: is the capital and the most populous city of the Indian state of Sikkim
at an elevation of 1,650 m (5,410 ft)
Temperatures range from an average maximum of 22 °C (72 °F ) in summertime to an average minimum of 5 °C (41 °F) in winter.

N_GT2.claim: Bagdogra airport is about 124 km — some five hours' drive — from Gangtok.

evidence.quote: Bagdogra , located 124 km (77 mi) (and a five-hour drive) away in the neighboring state of West Bengal

N_GT3.claim: MG Marg is the main promenade; Do-drul Chorten, Ganesh Tok and the Tashi Viewpoint, with views of Khangchendzonga, are classic stops.

evidence.quote: Take a stroll through MG Marg, the city's main promenade
Do-drul Chorten is marked by a golden dome
On clear days, visitors can enjoy stunning views of Mt. Khangchendzonga, Mt. Siniolchu , and the vibrant villages of North Sikkim from the Tashi Viewpoint.

N_GTN1.claim: The Namgyal Institute of Tibetology, about 5 km south in Deorali, holds the largest collection of Tibetan works outside Tibet.

evidence.quote: boasts the largest collection of Tibetan works outside Tibet. Located in Deorali, south of Gangtok, about 5 km away, it includes a museum, a research center, and a library.

N_GTN3.claim: Only Indian citizens may visit, Thursday to Sunday, with permits obtained a day ahead in Gangtok.

evidence.quote: On the Indian side, only citizens of India can visit the pass on Thursdays to Sundays, after obtaining permits one day in advance in Gangtok.

N_GTR1.claim: Rumtek, the Dharma Chakra Centre near Gangtok, is the seat in exile of the Karmapa, inaugurated in 1966.

evidence.quote: also called the Dharma Chakra Centre , is a gompa located in the Indian state of Sikkim near the capital Gangtok . It is the seat in exile of the Gyalwang Karmapa, inaugurated in 1966 by the 16th Karmapa.

N_GTT1.claim: Tsomgo (Changu) Lake lies at 12,313 ft and is sacred to the Sikkimese; open 7:30 am–4:30 pm, with yak rides.

evidence.quote: Perched at an altitude of 12,313 feet above sea level, Tsomgo Lake, also known as Changu Lake
it's a sacred site for the Sikkimese
There is a provision to take rides on yaks and mules here

N_GTT2.claim: Beyond the lake are the Kyongnosla Alpine Sanctuary, Nathu La and Hangu Lake.

evidence.quote: Beyond the lake, one can visit the Kyongnosla Alpine sanctuary, Nathu La Pass as well as Hangu Lake.

N_PL1.claim: Pelling, in West Sikkim at 2,150 m, has close views of the Kanchenjunga range.

evidence.quote: Standing at an elevation of 2,150 meters (7,050 feet), Pelling is a haven for nature lovers and adventure seekers.

N_PL2.claim: Nearby are the Rabdentse ruins, the former royal capital, the Tashiding Monastery and Yuksom, a trekking base.

evidence.quote: discover Rabdentse, the erstwhile royal capital hidden amidst ruins.
The Tashiding Monastery , nestled in the verdant hills of West Sikkim, is a revered pilgrimage site associated with Guru Padmasambhava
The nearby Yuksom Valley is a popular trekking destination

N_PLP1.claim: Pemayangtse, 'Perfect Sublime Lotus', became a monastery in 1705 and is Sikkim's second-oldest after Dubdi; open 8 am–4 pm.

evidence.quote: Pemayangtse translates to "Perfect Sublime Lotus"
Today, it is considered the second-oldest monastery in Sikkim, after Dubdi Monastery.

N_PLK1.claim: Khecheopalri Lake is revered as a wish-fulfilling lake by Buddhists and Hindus.

evidence.quote: The Khecheopalri Lake , also known as the "Wishing Lake," is revered by Buddhists and Hindus alike

N_PLN1.claim: Khangchendzonga National Park, a UNESCO site of 1,784 sq km, has 18 glaciers, including the 26 km Zemu Glacier, and 17 alpine lakes.

evidence.quote: This stunning park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site spread over 1784 square kilometres.
you'll be captivated by the sight of 18 glaciers, including the renowned Zemu Glacier (about 26 km long), and 17 shimmering alpine lakes

N_NS1.claim: Mangan is the gateway to North Sikkim and Gurudongmar Lake; Dzongu is a reserved area of the Lepcha community.

evidence.quote: Mangan serves as the gateway to the revered Gurudongmar Lake
Dzongu: A reserved area for the Lepcha community

N_NSL1.claim: Lachung, at about 9,600 ft, sits where the Lachen and Lachung rivers meet; visitors come October to May on the way to Yumthang.

evidence.quote: Lachung is at an elevation of about 9,600 feet (2,900 m) and at the confluence of the Lachen and Lachung Rivers
Tourists come from all over the world between October and May, mostly on their way to the Yumthang Valley

N_NSY1.claim: Yumthang, Sikkim's 'Valley of Flowers' at about 3,564 m, has hot springs and the Shingba Rhododendron Sanctuary; flowers bloom late February to mid June.

evidence.quote: The Yumthang Valley or Sikkim Valley of Flowers sanctuary , is a nature sanctuary with river, hot springs, yaks and grazing pasture
It is at an elevation of 3,564 metres (11,693 ft) above msl
The flowering season is from late February and to mid June

N_NSY2.claim: Yumthang is closed December to March due to heavy snow.

evidence.quote: Yumthang is closed between December and March due to heavy snowfall.

N_NSG1.claim: Gurudongmar Lake, at 5,430 m, is one of the highest lakes in the world, 190 km from Gangtok and about 5 km from the Chinese border.

evidence.quote: Gurudongmar Lake is one of the highest lakes in the world and in India , at an elevation of 5,430 m (17,800 ft) according to the Government of Sikkim
190 km (120 mi) from Gangtok , and about 5 km (3.1 mi) south of the Chinese border.

guides.title: How to reach Sikkim
guides.summary: Airports, railheads and the road up from Siliguri.
guides.seoTitle: How to Reach Sikkim: Bagdogra, NJP & Roads
guides.seoDescription: How to reach Sikkim: Bagdogra airport and New Jalpaiguri station, the road to Gangtok, and distances to Namchi and Ravangla.

body.intro: Sikkim is reached by road from the plains of North Bengal.

sections.heading: By air
sections.text: Bagdogra airport near Siliguri is the gateway; it is about 124 km — some five hours — from Gangtok. Pakyong airport has no operating flights at present.

sections.heading: By train
sections.text: New Jalpaiguri (NJP) is the main railhead, about 96 km from Namchi.

sections.heading: Onward
sections.text: Ravangla is 61 km from Gangtok and 120 km from Siliguri.

guides.title: Sikkim permits
guides.summary: Which areas need permits, and Nathu La's rules.
guides.seoTitle: Sikkim Permits: Restricted Areas & Nathu La
guides.seoDescription: Sikkim permits: restricted border areas, Nathu La for Indian citizens only (Thursday–Sunday), and permits for Tsomgo, North Sikkim and Zuluk.

body.intro: Much of Sikkim is a border area, so permits are part of every plan.

sections.heading: Restricted areas
sections.text: The Indian Army controls large border areas; many are restricted and need permits.

sections.heading: Nathu La
sections.text: Only Indian citizens may visit, Thursday to Sunday, with permits obtained a day ahead in Gangtok.

sections.heading: How
sections.text: Registered tour operators in Gangtok arrange most permits.

guides.title: Best time to visit Sikkim
guides.summary: Flowers, clear skies and the monsoon.
guides.seoTitle: Best Time to Visit Sikkim: Season Guide
guides.seoDescription: When to visit Sikkim: spring rhododendrons and Yumthang's flowers, monsoon landslides, Yumthang's winter closure and festival dates.

body.intro: Spring and autumn are the classic seasons; the monsoon brings landslides.

sections.heading: Spring
sections.text: Rhododendrons bloom across the state; Yumthang's flowers bloom late February to mid June.

sections.heading: Monsoon
sections.text: Heavy rain raises the risk of landslides that can cut off towns.

sections.heading: Winter
sections.text: Yumthang is closed December to March due to snow; Zuluk gets 3–5 ft of snow.

guides.title: North Sikkim guide: Lachen, Lachung and Gurudongmar
guides.summary: How the north is laid out, and what to expect.
guides.seoTitle: North Sikkim Guide: Lachen, Lachung, Gurudongmar
guides.seoDescription: North Sikkim: Chungthang's confluence, Lachen for Gurudongmar Lake (5,430 m), Lachung for Yumthang, and the Singba rhododendron sanctuary.

body.intro: The north splits at Chungthang into two valleys, each with its own highlights.

sections.heading: The fork
sections.text: At Chungthang the Lachen and Lachung rivers meet to form the Teesta.

sections.heading: Lachen side
sections.text: Lachen is the base for Gurudongmar Lake, one of the world's highest lakes.

sections.heading: Lachung side
sections.text: Lachung is the base for Yumthang, Sikkim's 'Valley of Flowers', and the Singba rhododendron sanctuary.

guides.title: Goecha La trek guide
guides.summary: What to know before trekking to Kanchenjunga's face.
guides.seoTitle: Goecha La Trek Guide: Yuksom to Kanchenjunga
guides.seoDescription: Planning the Goecha La trek: start at Yuksom, the national park, long days and acclimatisation.

body.intro: Sikkim's best-known trek starts in the old capital, Yuksom.

sections.heading: Start
sections.text: Yuksom, Sikkim's first capital, is the base for Kanchenjunga treks.

sections.heading: The pass
sections.text: Goecha La faces Kanchenjunga's south-east face; days are long and acclimatisation matters.

sections.heading: The park
sections.text: The route runs through Khangchendzonga National Park, a UNESCO site.

guides.title: Sikkim food and festivals
guides.summary: What to eat and when to catch the festivals.
guides.seoTitle: Sikkim Food & Festivals: Momos to Losar
guides.seoDescription: Sikkimese food — momos, thukpa, gundruk, Dalle Khorsani chilli — and festivals from Losar and Saga Dawa to Pang Lhabsol and Bumchu.

body.intro: Sikkim's food and festivals mix Tibetan, Nepali and Lepcha traditions.

sections.heading: Eat
sections.text: Momos, thukpa, gundruk, bamboo-shoot and millet dishes, yak-butter tea and the fiery Dalle Khorsani chilli.

sections.heading: Festivals
sections.text: Losar (Tibetan New Year), Saga Dawa, Pang Lhabsol for the guardian deities, and Tashiding's Bumchu around February–March.

guides.title: Adventure in Sikkim
guides.seoDescription: Adventure in Sikkim: Teesta rafting, paragliding and mountain biking, hiking in Fambong Lho and the Goecha La trek.

body.intro: Sikkim's rivers and mountains make it one of India's best adventure states.

sections.heading: On the water
sections.text: Teesta rafting suits beginners and experienced rafters.

sections.heading: On land
sections.text: Paragliding, hiking and mountain biking are popular; Fambong Lho, about 20 km from Gangtok, is good for hiking.

sections.heading: Big treks
sections.text: Goecha La from Yuksom faces Kanchenjunga.

guides.title: First-time visitor's guide to Sikkim
guides.summary: A simple plan for a first trip.
guides.seoTitle: First Time in Sikkim: What to Know
guides.seoDescription: A first-timer's guide to Sikkim: Gangtok, Tsomgo Lake, North Sikkim, West Sikkim's monasteries, permits and the plastic-bottle ban.

body.intro: Most first trips combine Gangtok, one high-altitude day and either the north or the west.

sections.heading: Gangtok
sections.text: The capital at 1,650 m, with MG Marg, monasteries and Tsomgo Lake as a day trip.

sections.heading: North or west
sections.text: North Sikkim for high lakes and valleys; West Sikkim for Pelling, Yuksom and the old monasteries.

sections.heading: Rules
sections.text: Many areas need permits, and plastic water bottles are banned.
